In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of a new default risk ratio, based on the fundamental analysis of the company, and its application in the structured-form model.

a theoretical and methodological analysis of the default risk ratio (DPR) and its application to a case study of a company listed on the Italian Stock Exchange (Borsa Italiana) in the period 2005-2010.

the following issues: (i) to define a default risk ratio (DPR) on the basis of firm’s fundamental analysis; (ii) to analyze how the DRR can be used in the structured-form credit risk models; (iii) to test the effectiveness of the DRR in a case study.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DRR can be considered as a new alternative tool for the financial analysis of the firm, which is able to define a new approach in the evaluation of the default risk, based on fundamental analysis rather than the market value of the assets.
the DRR, as a new tool, could be useful to define an innovative and more effective approach to the analysis of the default risk.

the DRR is a useful instrument for the firm’s management to define the optimal level of debt, and for the investors to define the optimal portfolio of investment, in the case of structured-form model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DRR is a ratio which tries to define a new approach to the analysis of the company capability to meet debt obligations by deriving it from the fundamental analysis of the company, instead of the volatility of the value of the assets on the market.
the DRR can be used as a useful tool for the risk management in the financial sector.

the DRR is a new alternative approach to define a new default probability model based on the firm fundamental analysis, rather than on the volatility of the market asset’s value, and it can be used in the structured-form default probability models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the default risk ratio (D.R.R.) can be considered as an alternative approach to analyze and to define the default risk of a firm.

the DRR can be used to evaluate the default risk of a firm in a more comprehensive way than the traditional approaches based on the volatility of the assets value, by monitoring the effects that the debt level has on the firm’s economic and financial dynamics.
the fundamental analysis can be a powerful tool for the credit rating process.
